name: OH-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Bob Latta running with large financial edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: Latta holds a heavily Republican seat, a huge fundraising advantage, and incumbency, while Shaver's campaign is essentially unfunded; markets price a Republican win near certainty. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based baseline with only a modest tilt toward the incumbent.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or a dramatic fundraising turnaround for Shaver would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Ohio's fifth district is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about twelve points toward the GOP, and Bob Latta has held the seat since 2007. He is running for another term with roughly $1.5 million raised and over $1 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Brian Shaver, has raised under $12,000 and has no meaningful outside support, leaving him little capacity to communicate with voters.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point strongly to Latta. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of winning. The expected margin is roughly sixteen points Republican, with the seat rated Likely R rather than Safe R only because of the usual uncertainty in low-information races.
